The SSL handshake failure (`CertPathValidatorException: Trust anchor for certification path not found`) occurred because Android (API 24+) does not trust custom or user certificate authorities by default. The development backend serves HTTPS using the self-signed certificate in `dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem`, but the app was not configured to trust this CA.

### Changes Made

1. **Copied the dev CA certificate to resources**:
   - Added [shelftap_dev_ca.pem](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-A-r3/work/app/src/main/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem) under `app/src/main/res/raw/` so the Android resource system can access it.

2. **Created Network Security Configuration**:
   - Added [network_security_config.xml](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-A-r3/work/app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml) under `app/src/main/res/xml/` with `<debug-overrides>` trusting both `@raw/shelftap_dev_ca` and `system` certificates during debug builds without compromising release security.

3. **Configured Manifest**:
   - Updated `<application>` in [AndroidManifest.xml](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-A-r3/work/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml#L6-L10) with `android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"`.
